rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's angels support a messenger and his companions, so although they face trials, they ultimately prevail and no enemy can defeat them.
rows.anchor: a whole army of God’s angels is at the support of a messenger and his companions, and none can defeat those which have such support.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orders to disregard the adversaries and observe them reassure the Prophet and urge him to wait patiently.
rows.anchor: These verses are meant to assure the Prophet (sws) and to urge him to wait and show patience.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to leave the adversaries' excesses unanswered until God completes the proof, leaving them no excuse; they will soon see their fate.
rows.anchor: so that God conclusively communicates the truth to them and they are left with no excuse to deny it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees demanded that punishment be hastened and claimed they would not believe until shown a sample of it.
rows.anchor: would say that unless they are shown a sample of it, they will not profess faith.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the punishment reaches their homes, it means doom and completely destroys the warned community of a messenger.
rows.anchor: When this punishment alights in their houses it will spell doom for those had been warned of it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Arab caravans were raided in the morning, ṣabāḥ came to connote attack and raids, a sense also carried by the proclamation here.
rows.anchor: the word صباح connotes attack and raids.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing warning repeats the assurance of 37:174-175: the Prophet should wait, while disbelievers will soon witness what they were told.
rows.anchor: the topic of assurance and warning is repeated that was discussed earlier in verses 174-175

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God, the true master of power and sovereignty, is exalted above everything the idolaters falsely ascribe to Him.
rows.anchor: the real master of all power and sovereignty – beyond all things these Idolaters ascribe to Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has exposed the idolaters' baseless views and consequences; if they persist, they will face their fate.
rows.anchor: if they now do not desist from these things, they will see their fate.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As earlier prophets received peace after their accounts, Muhammad receives the same glad tidings at the end of this sūrah.
rows.anchor: after the mention of the anecdotes of other prophets earlier, each was given the glad tidings of peace here at the end

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The established divine practice for all messengers also applies to Muhammad: messengers receive peace and their enemies are destroyed.
rows.anchor: the established practice of God which has materialized for all His messengers stands true for him as well

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone deserves thanks and praise.
rows.anchor: God alone is worthy of being thanked and praised.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the struggle between truth and falsehood, God will make truth prevail and defeat falsehood.
rows.anchor: He will definitely make the truth prevail and defeat falsehood.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Lord of the universe, God requires justice in this world and the next; this providence grounds praise and gratitude in both.
rows.anchor: the requisite of this state of His that justice prevail in this world as well as in that to come.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercession remains under God's control; the Prophet should entrust these people to God and pray for them.
rows.anchor: consign the matter of such people to God and is also advised to pray for them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrogant attribute God-given wealth and status to their own planning, though earlier people held the same delusion and were seized without their plans helping them.
rows.anchor: they think that the wealth and status which God has bestowed upon them is the result of their own planning

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since wealth and sustenance are God's gifts, everyone must thank Him; gratitude is part of tawḥīd.
rows.anchor: Wealth and sustenance is a gift of God. Hence thanking Him is imperative on every one

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than despairing of God or seeking deities and intercessors, people should turn to the forgiving and merciful God in every circumstance.
rows.anchor: losing hope in God and seeking other deities and intercessors is not the correct way.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should turn to God and believe in His revealed Book before He seizes them; later regret and a wish to believe will be too late.
rows.anchor: before He seizes them, people should turn to Him and profess faith in this magnificent Book

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing section establishes that God alone is worshipped, creates everything, and holds the keys of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: He alone is the Creator of everything and the keys of the heavens and the earth are in His jurisdiction

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and earlier prophets were taught that associating partners with God makes people's deeds come to nothing.
rows.anchor: the deeds of people who set up partners with God will come to nothing

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the trumpet sounds, people fall unconscious and rise at its second sounding; the earth shines, records open, witnesses appear, and judgment is fair.
rows.anchor: when the trumpet is sounded everyone will fall down unconscious. And when the trumpet is sounded again everyone will rise up

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing verses depict the respective fates of Hell's and Paradise's inhabitants.
rows.anchor: details of the circumstances of the dwellers of Hell and Paradise are depicted.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question makes the arrogant people's deserving of Hell so obvious that no one could disagree; they will be cast there.
rows.anchor: such haughty people are worthy of Hell

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In contrast, those who feared God are taken to a secure abode where neither harm nor grief reaches them.
rows.anchor: neither will they be harmed nor will they be grieved.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ marks location, while mafāzah means security or success and refers to Paradise.
rows.anchor: indicates the locus and the word means

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise frees its people from regrets about the past and fears about the future.
rows.anchor: They will be secure from all the regrets of the past

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not leave the world unattended after creating it; as its guardian, He deserves His servants' trust.
rows.anchor: in fact, He is the protector of all and for this reason all His people should trust Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God holds the keys to the heavens and earth, and worldly provision and afterlife rewards are His favors.
rows.anchor: the keys of all the treasures of the heavens and the earth are with Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who reject God's revelations and persist in polytheism lose and themselves suffer its consequences.
rows.anchor: they themselves will face the evil consequences of this foolishness – no one else.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final section first has the Prophet ask why people demand worship of others despite the clear facts and the revealed warning against polytheism.
rows.anchor: Coming up are the closing verses of this sūrah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet asks why idolaters demand worship of others despite clear facts and the revelation that polytheists' deeds are wasted.
rows.anchor: why they ask him to worship others besides God in spite of all these clear facts

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters fail to grasp God's majesty and associate baseless things with His divinity, leaving them unafraid of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: they are associating such things with the divinity of God which are baseless and on their basis have no fear of the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's majesty is shown in the two trumpet blasts: all fall unconscious, rise again, then face judgment with the record opened and prophets and witnesses present.
rows.anchor: when His trumpet is sounded everyone in the heavens and the earth will become unconscious

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final section presents the fates of Paradise's and Hell's inhabitants to wake those who indulge in complacent hopes.
rows.anchor: so that the eyes of those who are having sweet dreams are opened.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author begins defining jāhil as a person who fails to use knowledge and intellect; the sentence continues across the page break.
rows.anchor: refers to a person who instead of using his knowledge and

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jāhil here describes one led by emotions and desires instead of knowledge and intellect.
rows.anchor: intellect is led by emotions and desires.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the evidence that God created all and controls the keys to everything, the verse asks whether idolaters still demand that the Prophet worship their idols.
rows.anchor: even after these clear facts would they keep demanding from him to worship their idols

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question refers to idolaters' threat that the Prophet would incur their idols' wrath if he did not stop opposing ancestral religion.
rows.anchor: the Idolaters would try to strike the fear of their Idols

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the idolaters' demand is absurd, God addresses the Prophet and indirectly conveys to them that revelation to him and earlier prophets condemned polytheism.
rows.anchor: instead, the Prophet (sws) is addressed and these people are indirectly conveyed the message which the verse states

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheism makes even deeds done for God fruitless; God accepts good deeds only from servants who do not associate partners with Him.
rows.anchor: with polytheism whatever deeds are done even for God go waste and do not bear any fruit.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude to God is fulfilled only through worshipping Him alone; associating partners means a person is ungrateful and destroys the whole structure of religiosity.
rows.anchor: showing gratitude to Him is fulfilled only when He worships God alone.
